review_method: Distinct question-first AI derivation, followed by frozen reference, rubric, source and bounded neighbor comparison.

G1s.reasoning: A two-site rotation preserves the pair mass and every coordinate outside the pair. Thus it can change only the prefix at its own edge. Taking consecutive differences and appending both zero boundary differences recovers the converse local mass conditions. On a positive-radius pair the dot and determinant coefficients rotate each actual signed input to the nonnegative square roots of the two requested populations. The zero pair remains zero. Equal data admit every location. The examples give edge (1,2) and no edge, respectively. The authored reference, rubric and necessity/sufficiency joins agree with this derivation.
limitations: Exact normalized populations on a line and arbitrary real angles are essential. The angle can vary with the signed input, and the experiment cannot identify unobserved output signs.

LA101 and SP001 assess the signed local rotation algebra, SP005 assesses a squared-mass identity, and LA104 assesses invariant outside coordinates. Workbook A4 and B2 share the rotation or phase setting. G1s requires the additional inverse problem of finding all compatible locations. Local fragments overlap public test material, and the three local-rotation questions share exposure.
The cited declarations justify the pair orbit and fixed outside coordinates. The population model and the inverse prefix test are natural-language mathematics.
grading_notes: Accept the direct pair-mass and outside-coordinate criterion with its equivalence to the prefix test. A polar-angle or equal-radius rotation argument earns the same realization credit as the reference coefficients.

G2s.reasoning: Every cut inside the smallest interval containing the source and target support has a zero-initialized far side with positive target mass. Omitting that cut keeps that side zero, so the distinct required cuts give an additive lower bound against arbitrary circuits. In reverse, a leaf rotation can place the nonnegative pair norm at either parent orientation. One pass leaves the positive source coordinate and reversing the rotations gives the signed target. The degenerate positive/negative singleton cases cost zero or one when an incident edge exists, with the negative singleton unreachable at one site. The example needs five edges and any source in the support interval ties for optimality. The current map's cut join correctly uses squared mass, independently of signs.
limitations: The exact signed coordinate target counts a common-sign reversal. The gate count measures arbitrary real adjacent coordinate rotations on one specified input, with no auxiliary coordinate or native-gate synthesis claim.

LA101 and LA104 assess signed local elimination and persistence of zeros, LA103 inverse chronological replay, and LA119/LA203 counts of specified implementations. Workbook B1/B3 treat a fixed chronological construction or precision allocation. The universal source-and-support cut bound and matching optimal construction distinguish G2s within this comparison.

The graph declaration Step provides the adjacent index rule and carries a partial route status in the frozen graph. It does not establish an optimization theorem. Local rotation, orthogonality and list inversion facts support the worked natural-language proof.
grading_notes: Accept forward signed subtree-mass distribution or inverse leaf elimination when orientations and final signs are justified. The worked eight-site gate list is optional. A projective identification of the two source-only signs fails the stated exact-vector convention.

G3s.reasoning: Propagate potential support only across a matching edge with a previously marked endpoint. Two unmarked zeros cannot become nonzero and later cancellation cannot enlarge support beyond those marks. The squared overlap is bounded by marked target weight. First contacts form parent-child edges at strictly increasing times down each branch. Reversing these contacts compresses the signed normalized projection to the positive root whenever a merge is present, and empty or zero-mass cases are handled at score level. Sort the recurrence by subtree, assigning each contacted child to one distinct slot and evaluating it with the residual budget. Disjoint sibling subtrees realize the matching sum. The distance-two example has scores zero, one half and one, with contention at the first root contact. The rubric separates support, projection, attainable signed synthesis, matching optimization and finite-work justification.
limitations: Layer depth counts endpoint-disjoint rotations on coordinate sites. Polynomiality is in tree size and the integer layer budget measured numerically, under unit-cost real operations and comparisons. No finite-bit or primitive-wire bound is certified.

Workbook A3 shares projection/normalization, G2 shares mass and fidelity bookkeeping for a fixed approximate map sequence, and LA213 treats scheduling depth for fixed primitive gates. LA101/LA104 and SP005 supply local elimination and mass facts. The dynamic reachable-support projection and optimized contact schedule are additional reasoning obligations.

Source declarations support only the exact local rotations, pair norms and inverses. The temporal tree argument and sharp optimization are natural-language results. Radius and static edge colorings cannot replace the scheduling proof.
grading_notes: Accept matching, flow or an equivalent polynomial recurrence with both inequalities, and accept forward signed splitting when legal. If only the negative projected singleton direction matches, the positive source has the required squared score.

C1s.reasoning: Acting on the input basis column, the first gate routes x to p(x) with weight a(x) and the second contributes b(p(x)) and q(p(x)). Comparing coefficients gives the unique input table f composed with p. The unit ratio f(p(x))/f(x) must be the same for every column for projective equality, and must equal one for exact equality. In control-first CNOT, a control-zero column fixes that common scalar to one, and a control-one moved column tests exp(i theta). Independently, the balanced input (|01>+|11>)/sqrt(2) at theta=pi gives one symmetric and one antisymmetric output on |01> and |10>, up to common signs. Basis probes still see the same routed label because all nonzero weights have modulus one. The reference's alternate basis pair is equally valid. The authored route correctly joins the general table rule with the CNOT data and keeps the output-probability statement on basis inputs.
limitations: BE111 (public test) already assesses the same single-surviving-term composition with weights one. LA016 (public test) assesses the exact/projective/coherent distinction for a two-dimensional rotation. LA013 and BE104 (train), plus workbook B2 and P1, supply related relabeling and phase mechanisms. None of these inspected neighbors asks the complete phase-table pullback, all-angle CNOT test and orthogonality construction together.

The source theorems certify the basis formulas and chronological product. The rewrite criterion and orthogonality argument are independently checked natural-language deductions. Arbitrary finite-label routing and a distinct-wire CNOT use different source interfaces.

The CNOT is an involution, so its concrete table is insufficient to grade the general pullback direction. The ratio being a root of unity on each cycle is a necessary compatibility constraint for a common ratio, not a substitute for checking the actual ratios on all columns.
grading_notes: Award witness credit for any normalized two-term input with equal probabilities on opposite control sectors at theta=pi and a verified zero output overlap. Either orientation of the global scalar is acceptable when used consistently.

C2s.reasoning: Set r_x=b_x/a_x. The calibration equation propagates d_{p(x)}=r_x d_x. Transport along the directed arcs forces closure and the pinned ratios. On a pinned cycle choose one pin to specify the base phase, then compare every other pin by its forward arc. On an unpinned cycle choose one arbitrary unit phase. This constructs all solutions because the cycle recurrence determines them from the base and leaves the last edge satisfied exactly by closure. Fixed points satisfy r_x=1 with their phase either pinned or free. Independent three-cycle exhibit: p=(1 2 3), a=(1,1,1), b=(-1,i,i), and d_1=d_2=1. The product is one in both tables, but the first directed edge forces d_2=-1. Equal labeled cycle products are complete only for the unpinned case. The construction step in the supplied DAG joins transport, closure, and pin tests; the latter tests become vacuous with zero or one pin.
limitations: PLAN313 (public test) classifies phase-free cycles under arbitrary permutation conjugation. BE108 and LA013 (train) involve basis reindexing, and workbook C2 supplies neighboring gauge cancellation with fixed ends. A labeled weighted cycle with prescribed vertex phases has different admissible transformations and an extra endpoint check.

The source fixes the weighted matrix and composition convention. It does not establish the cycle invariant, complete parametrization, or pin obstruction. All conclusions concern exact diagonal conjugation with the same known permutation and unit-modulus weights.

The phase-free shared composition from BE111 and the pullback/coherent distinctions used in C1s should remain grouped as exposure, while the reference-arc transport defines the additional C2s operation.
grading_notes: Checking every pair of pins is optional. Checking one base pin against all other pins suffices once closure is proved. Additive phase differences modulo 2 pi or any equivalent spanning-path construction meet the same rubric.

C3s.reasoning: On a cycle of length ell, powers return to the starting label exactly at multiples of ell, producing the phase h_C raised to the quotient of the power by ell and ell equal diagonal contributions. The cyclic basis gives the factor z^ell-h_C. In increasing order, the n=ell trace equation subtracts already recovered proper divisors and leaves ell times the single unknown value on the known cycle. Independent six-label ambiguity: fixed products (1,-1) and transposition products (1,-1) can be replaced by fixed products (i,-i) and transposition products (1,1); each product is realizable by a single weighted edge. Both spectra come from (z^2-1)^2(z^2+1). Equivalently odd traces vanish, and in both assignments t_(2k)=4+2*(-1)^k. Each projected trace divided by ell is a power sum of the products on that length. Newton's identities recover the monic root polynomial with multiplicities, and every within-length reassignment is realizable. All labels at a length are determined exactly when its recovered multiset is constant. The final joined route combines recovery with realizability to establish that boundary.
limitations: PLAN108 and PLAN109 (public test) use trace invariance or character-based reconstruction, PLAN313 uses permutation cycle type, and PLAN415 separates spectrum estimation from fixed-state outcome preservation. Workbook P1 uses one cyclic-shift eigenvector and C3 propagates Gram/inner-product data. These are exposed foundations. None of the inspected full contracts asks for this cross-length characteristic-polynomial collision or length-sector recovery with the remaining label ambiguity.

The source multiplication theorem grounds iteration with the same operand order. Characteristic factors, trace inversion, projected power sums and assignment ambiguity are natural-language deductions. Data are exact complex numbers with known permutation and cycle counts. The question makes no numerical stability, approximate-spectrum, or efficient measurement assertion.

The Phase II revision changes a boundary label only, correctly attributing the repeated root to the polynomial reconstructed from sector power sums. Equal-length shuffling alone is insufficient for the separate global-trace counterexample.
grading_notes: Accept a valid common characteristic polynomial or an explicit equality of all traces, provided the construction changes a product multiset at a fixed length. For distinct lengths, a Newton reconstruction of the reciprocal characteristic polynomial with least-degree factor removal is an equivalent constructive solution.
